sections.h2: Which Crisp County offices deal with a property tax bill?
sections.html:
In Crisp County two separate offices share the work. One office collects county and school tax. The other, run by the appraisal staff in Cordele, sets values. Elected county commissioners then adopt the millage rates that turn a value into a bill.

State revenue officials list crispcountytax.com as the collector's web address and crispcounty.com for the appraisers and commissioners. The county's administrative building is at 210 S. 7th Street in Cordele, and the appraisal staff answer at (229) 276-2635. For the commissioner's counter hours, payment options and your exact balance, ask the Crisp County tax commissioner directly.

County commissioners meet in Room 305 of the Government Center every second Tuesday morning, at nine. The county says that board adopts the budget and sets the property tax rate, so that meeting is where a rate debate plays out.

sections.h2: What is Crisp County, GA, and why does its geography matter to sellers?
sections.html:
Crisp County covers 281 square miles in south central Georgia, of which 8.4 are water. Cordele is both the courthouse town and the lone city. Arabi is a town, Wenona a census-designated place and Coney an unincorporated community. The whole county makes up the Cordele micropolitan area.

Two river systems share the land. The western two thirds drains to the middle Flint River, and the eastern third belongs to the Alapaha River basin of the Suwannee. Interstate 75 crosses it, as do U.S. 41, U.S. 280 and State Routes 33, 90, 257 and 300. Lawmakers carved the county out of Dooly in August 1905.

Neighbors are Dooly to the north, Wilcox to the east, Turner to the southeast, Worth to the southwest, and Lee and Sumter to the west. A county water notice also mentions the Lake Blackshear area water system, which serves customers across Crisp, Sumter and Worth counties, which is a detail for sellers near the water to confirm with the utility.

sections.h2: What do the latest Census estimates say about Crisp County homes?
sections.html:
Crisp County lost more residents than any of the four counties in this QuickFacts comparison. Census takers counted 23,439 people in 2010 and 20,128 in 2020. The newest estimate, 19,237, means a further slide of 4.4 percent.

  • Housing units, July 2025: 9,989 against 7,908 households.
  • Owner-occupied share: 55.5 percent, the smallest of any county in the comparison.
  • Value of the typical owned home in the 2020 to 2024 survey: $140,200.
  • Rent for the typical rental unit: $778 per month.
  • Share of residents in poverty: 22.8 percent.
  • Household income at the midpoint: $45,105.
  • Permits for new housing in 2025: 27.

The numbers describe a market with lower home values than any of its three comparison counties and few new permits. Rents run lower than elsewhere in the set, a point for anyone weighing whether to keep the house as a rental.

sections.h2: What jobs and commutes shape Crisp County housing demand?
sections.html:
Crisp County residents drive an average of 20.6 minutes to work, the shortest trip among the four counties in the same QuickFacts comparison. The county reports 503 employer establishments employing 7,557 people in 2023, a 2.3 percent decline from 2022.

Health care and social assistance brought in about $168.5 million in 2022, the largest service line listed. Retail sales that year were about $570 million, which works out to $28,902 per resident. Transportation and warehousing receipts were about $48.3 million.

Short drives and a base of health care and retail jobs mean many buyers will be local households. The county Assessors can show recent sales on your street.

sections.h2: What dates control a Crisp County property tax year?
sections.html:
Georgia's county fact sheet for Crisp County sets the rhythm of the year. The table gathers each rule it states.

Crisp County property tax calendar and rules (source: Georgia Department of Revenue county fact sheet)
ItemRule on the fact sheet
Returns of propertyJanuary 1 through April 1, filed with the county tax office
Homestead applicationAny time, up to April 1 of the first year of the exemption
Official bill due dateDecember 20, unless the county adopts December 1, November 15 or installments
Interest grace60 days from the postmark of the bill
Assessment appealPostmarked within 45 days of the notice mailing
Refund claimWithin three years of payment
Mobile home permitWithin 30 days of placement, then January 1 to April 1 yearly

A county can pick an earlier date, so the one on your bill governs. Phone the tax commissioner to confirm it before fixing a closing day.

sections.h2: How do I question a Crisp County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the assessment notice. Your challenge goes to the Board of Tax Assessors rather than the collector, and the state sheet requires a postmark no more than 45 days after the notice was sent.

The Assessors' office publishes a standing notice that appraisal staff may visit parcels during the digest year to measure structures, list construction details and photograph the property. If an appraiser visits, ask what changed in the record. Tell the office about repairs, water damage or an unfinished room that lowers value, since the record is built from what the county has on file.

  • Last day to file a return describing your own view of value: April 1.
  • Questions about a review notice: (229) 276-2635.
  • Put the appeal on paper and keep a postmarked copy.
  • A claim for tax paid in error has to begin within three years of the payment.

sections.h2: How does the Crisp County millage process work?
sections.html:
Rates in Crisp County are adopted by the Board of Commissioners for county tax and by the school board for school tax. When a county plans to collect more than the rollback rate, Georgia requires public hearings. The Crisp County public notices page lists the 2026 current tax digest along with a five-year history of levy.

That page also carries hearing letters for zoning matters and election notices. A seller who plans to list should compare the five-year levy history with the bill on the house, because buyers will ask what the yearly tax runs.

The county site does not give a bill amount for any parcel. Ask the Assessors for the value on file and the tax commissioner for the millage that applies.

sections.h2: What if the seller of a Crisp County house still owes tax?
sections.html:
Get a payoff statement from the tax commissioner and have the settlement agent pay it out of the sale proceeds. Clearing the balance at closing keeps the county bill from following the house to the buyer.

  • Cities levy their own tax and the state sheet says the city clerk bills it, so a house inside Cordele or Arabi may carry a second bill. Ask whether either city's tax is collected with the county's.
  • A mobile home needs a location permit within 30 days of being set in place, renewed each winter before April 1.
  • A buyer's lender has 90 days to record a long-term security instrument, with intangible tax of $1.50 per $500 of the note, usually collected by the superior court clerk.

An heir selling an inherited Crisp County house should gather the last bill, confirm whether a homestead exemption was on file, and ask the Assessors whether a new application is needed in the heir's name.

faqs.q: Which office takes Crisp County property tax payments?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner, whose website the state lists as crispcountytax.com. Ask that office for counter hours, payment methods and your balance.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Crisp County valuation?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the assessment notice is mailed. Send it to the Board of Tax Assessors with a postmark inside that window.

faqs.q: How long is the interest-free window after a Crisp County bill is mailed?
faqs.a: Georgia gives 60 days from the postmark on the bill before interest starts, although late balances can still pick up penalties. The official due date is December 20 unless the county has chosen an earlier one.

faqs.q: Is Crisp County growing or shrinking?
faqs.a: Shrinking. Counts fell from 23,439 in 2010 to 20,128 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate sits at 19,237.

faqs.q: What is the typical home price in Crisp County?
faqs.a: Federal survey data for 2020 to 2024 shows $140,200 as the value of the typical owner-occupied house. Individual sales can land above or below it.
